**Simplify:**
$$(1-p)^n + np(1-p)^{n-1} = \frac{3}{16}$$

**Factor:**
$$(1-p)^{n-1}[(1-p) + np] = \frac{3}{16}$$

$$(1-p)^{n-1}[1 - p + np] = \frac{3}{16}$$

$$(1-p)^{n-1}[1 + p(n-1)] = \frac{3}{16}$$

**Test values:** Assuming independence and equal likelihood suggests p = 1/2:

$$(1/2)^{n-1}[1 + (n-1)/2] = \frac{3}{16}$$

$$(1/2)^{n-1} \cdot \frac{n+1}{2} = \frac{3}{16}$$

$$(1/2)^n(n+1) = \frac{3}{16}$$
